text: If a man ever tries to use the argument on you that women were just were built to create babies, ask him about menopause. There's only three animals in nature that have menopause. We are one of them. The only biological purpose for that is that we need to pass on knowledge. Men can keep producing sperm until they die, i.e. you guys were actually born just to procreate, not us. That's your purpose. Look, guys, let me start with this. Any man who genuinely thinks that women were just built to make babies is either profoundly ignorant or simply not very bright. But then this lady correctly condemns that terrible viewpoint only to say that men were actually born just to procreate and that this is our purpose. So you condemn reducing women to their reproductive organs and then immediately reduce men to theirs? Now it is men who were built only to make babies? How did we get here? And honestly, this is a good example of how many arguments work online today. People condemn a particular group for doing something terrible, but instead of rejecting the behavior itself, they apparently just want the opportunity to reverse the target and do exactly the same thing back. But OK, she also made quite a few scientific claims, so let's check some of them. Claim 1. Only three animals have menopause. This is outdated. A 2024 nature study identifies prolonged post-reproductive lifespans in five species of toothed whale. Kilo whales, short fin pilot whales, false kilo whales, belugas, and narwhals. A 2023 science paper also found demographic and hormonal evidence of menopause in one wild chimpanzee population, although researchers are still debating how representative that population is. So menopause is rare in nature, but only three animals is no longer accurate. Claim 2. The only biological purpose of menopause is passing on knowledge. Passing on knowledge may be part of the explanation, but saying it is the only purpose is far too confident. The grandmother hypothesis proposes that older women could improve the survival and reproductive success of their descendants by providing food, child care, protection, and knowledge. Research on whales similarly suggests that older females can help their children and grandchildren survive. But researchers also discuss reduced reproductive competition between generations, the increased dangers of giving birth at older ages, and possible biological limits on how long mammalian eggs remain viable. There's still debate about how these different explanations fit together. So older females can help their descendants is a serious evolutionary hypothesis. Science has proven that the only biological purpose of menopause is to pass on knowledge is not. Claim 3. Men produce sperm until they die. Some men can remain fertile into old age, and men do not experience a universal abrupt reproductive ending equivalent to a menopause. But sperm production and fertility do not simply remain unchanged until death. Research finds age-related decline in semen volume, sperm movement, normal sperm shape, and sperm DNA quality. Some elderly men can father children, many cannot. And even if every man produced perfect sperm until his final breath, that still wouldn't prove that reproduction is his sole purpose. That conclusion simply does not logically follow. So let's return to the main point. Saying women are just built to make babies is dehumanizing nonsense. Saying men are just built to make babies is exactly the same dehumanizing nonsense with the sexes reversed. So you did not defeat the terrible argument. You copied it and changed the target.
